subject: Communication
title: The Johari Window: Blind Spots
description: Learn The Johari Window: Blind Spots in one minute.

hook.text: You have traits everyone sees but you don't. You have traits nobody sees. The Johari Window maps these hidden zones.

buildup.text: Four quadrants: Open (known to you and others), Blind (known to others, not you), Hidden (known to you, not others).

discovery.text: Self-awareness means shrinking the Blind quadrant — seeing yourself as others see you, not just as you imagine yourself.

twist.text: Research shows 95% of people think they're self-aware, but only 10-15% actually are. The gap is enormous.

climax.text: Feedback from trusted others is the primary way to reduce blind spots. Self-reflection alone isn't enough.

punchline.text: You can't fix what you can't see. And you can't see it alone.

quiz.question: What percentage of people are genuinely self-aware, according to research?

details.summary: The Johari Window is a four-quadrant model of self-knowledge: open (known to you and others), blind (known to others but not you), hidden (known to you but not others), and unknown (known to neither). Emotional intelligence growth means shrinking the blind and hidden quadrants.
details.whyItMatters: The Johari Window reveals that significant parts of your behavior are visible to everyone except you. Feedback shrinks your blind spot and improves communication.
takeaways: Four quadrants: open, blind, hidden, and unknown
Feedback reduces the blind spot quadrant

faq.question: How do you reduce your blind spot effectively?
faq.answer: Ask trusted colleagues and friends for specific behavioral feedback. Use 360-degree assessments. Record yourself in meetings and watch the playback. Notice patterns in how others react to you. The blind spot shrinks only through external input, never through introspection alone.

faq.question: When is it appropriate to expand the hidden quadrant?
faq.answer: Some information is appropriately private. Strategic self-disclosure builds trust but oversharing can be counterproductive. The goal is not total transparency but authentic connection. Share what serves the relationship and keeps important emotions from festering in secrecy.
